hypotheses.justification: This is the Gaussian Poincaré inequality, independent of a Clark–Ocone family. The definitions identify mderiv with the Cameron–Martin gradient and D12 with its graph-closure domain. A replacement proof uses Gaussian interpolation: for independent X,Y with law P and mean m, put Y_t = m + t(X-m) + √(1-t²)(Y-m). Gaussian integration by parts gives Var(f(X)) = ∫₀¹ E⟨Df(X),Df(Y_t)⟩ dt for smooth bounded f. This calculation can be established first in finite-dimensional Gaussian coordinates and then by approximation; the library provides Gaussian integration by parts as integral_inner_mderiv. Since Y_t also has law P, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the integral by E‖Df(X)‖². Finally, inGraphClosure_mderivClosure supplies smooth bounded approximants converging to F and its derivative; continuity of expectation and norms passes the inequality to F. No inverse covariance is used, so singular Gaussian laws are covered; for a Dirac law the centered norm is zero. IsGaussian already makes P a probability measure, excluding the zero-measure case.
